The report is filled in milestone by milestone. All data are synthetic (Synthea).
No clinical conclusion may be drawn from them.

```{r}
library(gt)

results <- function(file) read.csv(file.path("..", "results", file))

row_counts  <- results("m1_row_counts.csv")
obs_periods <- results("m1_observation_periods.csv")
zero        <- results("m1_concept_id_zero.csv")
dq          <- results("m1_dq_checks.csv")
drug_dups   <- results("m1_drug_duplicate_detail.csv")

n_rows <- function(table) row_counts$n_rows[row_counts$table_name == table]
failing <- function(check, table) {
  dq$rows_failing[dq$check_name == check & dq$table_name == table]
}
share <- function(check, table) {
  dq$share_failing[dq$check_name == check & dq$table_name == table]
}
pct <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * x)
num <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",")
```

## Data exploration and quality (M1)

### Row counts

```{r}
gt(row_counts) |>
  cols_label(table_name = "Table", n_rows = "Rows", n_persons = "Persons") |>
  fmt_integer(columns = c(n_rows, n_persons))
```

The `measurement` table holds `r num(n_rows("measurement"))` rows and the
`observation` table `r num(n_rows("observation"))`. Nothing in this project can use
laboratory values or observations from them.

### Observation periods

Every person has `r ifelse(obs_periods$n_persons_with_more_than_one_period == 0, "exactly one", "at least one")`
observation period. The median length is `r num(obs_periods$median_length_days)` days.
`r obs_periods$n_zero_length_periods` periods start and end on the same day.
These people can never meet the 365 days of prior observation required in M3.

### Unmapped records

```{r}
gt(zero) |>
  cols_label(
    table_name = "Table", concept_column = "Concept column",
    n_rows = "Rows", n_concept_zero = "concept_id = 0",
    share_concept_zero = "Share"
  ) |>
  fmt_integer(columns = c(n_rows, n_concept_zero)) |>
  fmt_percent(columns = share_concept_zero, decimals = 2) |>
  sub_missing(missing_text = "empty table")
```

### Data-quality checks

Failing rows are counted and reported. The data are not changed.

```{r}
gt(dq[, c("check_name", "rule", "table_name", "rows_checked",
          "rows_failing", "share_failing")]) |>
  cols_label(
    check_name = "Check", rule = "Rule", table_name = "Table",
    rows_checked = "Rows checked", rows_failing = "Rows failing",
    share_failing = "Share"
  ) |>
  fmt_integer(columns = c(rows_checked, rows_failing)) |>
  fmt_percent(columns = share_failing, decimals = 2)
```

`r pct(share("duplicate_records", "drug_exposure"))` of drug records
(`r num(failing("duplicate_records", "drug_exposure"))` rows) repeat an earlier
row with the same person, drug, start date and type. They fall into
`r num(drug_dups$n_duplicate_groups)` groups of up to
`r drug_dups$max_rows_in_one_group` rows. Within a group the rows differ in
visit in `r drug_dups$groups_differing_in_visit` groups, in end date in
`r drug_dups$groups_differing_in_end_date`, in start time in
`r drug_dups$groups_differing_in_start_time`, in quantity in
`r drug_dups$groups_differing_in_quantity` and in source value in
`r drug_dups$groups_differing_in_source_value`. On the columns compared they
are copies. They do not move the date of a first treatment. They would
inflate any count of drug exposures.

`r failing("events_outside_observation", "condition_occurrence")` condition
records start outside the person's observation period.

## Concept sets and terminology mapping (M2)

```{r}
codelist_summary <- results("m2_codelist_summary.csv")
review           <- results("m2_breast_cancer_review.csv")
bc_counts        <- results("m2_breast_cancer_counts.csv")
treatment_counts <- results("m2_treatment_counts.csv")
mapping          <- results("m2_source_to_standard.csv")
icd              <- results("m2_icd_vocabularies.csv")
not_found        <- results("m2_ingredients_not_found.csv")
bc_definition    <- read.csv(file.path("..", "codelists", "breast_cancer_definition.csv"))
icd10cm_map      <- read.csv(file.path("..", "codelists", "breast_cancer_icd10cm_map.csv"))

icd_row <- function(id) icd[icd$vocabulary_id == id, ]
```

Every concept was found by a query saved in `sql/codelists/`. No concept_id is
typed by hand. The vocabulary version is `r bc_definition$vocabulary_version[1]`.

### Concept sets

The breast cancer set is the SNOMED concept
"`r bc_definition$concept_name`" and all its descendants. The drug sets are the
descendants of RxNorm ingredients listed by name in
`codelists/treatment_classes_input.csv`.
`r if (nrow(not_found) == 0) "Every listed ingredient was found." else paste("Not found:", paste(not_found$ingredient_name, collapse = ", "))`

```{r}
gt(codelist_summary) |>
  cols_label(codelist_name = "Codelist", class = "Class",
             n_concepts = "Concepts", n_flagged_for_review = "Flagged for review") |>
  fmt_integer(columns = n_concepts) |>
  sub_missing(missing_text = "")
```

The hierarchy below the parent also holds concepts that are not primary breast
cancer. They stay in the set and are flagged by a name rule in
`R/20_codelists.R`.

```{r}
gt(review) |>
  cols_label(review_reason = "Reason", n_concepts = "Concepts")
```

Only `r nrow(bc_counts)` concept of the set occurs in the data,
"`r bc_counts$concept_name[1]`", in `r num(bc_counts$n_persons[1])` people.
The flagged concepts therefore change nothing in this dataset. They would matter
in real data.

### Treatment among people with breast cancer

People with a breast cancer record at any time, and their drug records from each
class at any time. These counts are not yet tied to the index date, which M3 sets.
Record counts include the duplicate drug rows found in M1.

```{r}
classes <- treatment_counts[treatment_counts$level == "class",
                            c("class", "n_persons", "n_records")]
gt(classes) |>
  cols_label(class = "Class", n_persons = "Persons", n_records = "Records") |>
  fmt_integer(columns = c(n_persons, n_records))
```

### Source to standard

```{r}
gt(mapping) |>
  cols_label(
    table_name = "Table", source_vocabulary_id = "Source vocabulary",
    standard_vocabulary_id = "Standard vocabulary", n_records = "Records",
    n_source_concepts = "Source concepts", n_standard_concepts = "Standard concepts",
    n_source_equals_standard = "Source is standard",
    n_confirmed_by_maps_to = "Confirmed by Maps to"
  ) |>
  fmt_integer(columns = starts_with("n_"))
```

Synthea records conditions in SNOMED and drugs in RxNorm. Both are already
standard, so here every source concept maps to itself.

### ICD-10

WHO ICD-10 is `r ifelse(icd_row("ICD10")$loaded == "yes", "loaded", "not loaded")`
in this vocabulary. ICD-10-CM is `r ifelse(icd_row("ICD10CM")$loaded == "yes", "loaded", "not loaded")`
(`r icd_row("ICD10CM")$vocabulary_version`, `r num(icd_row("ICD10CM")$n_concepts)` concepts).
The data hold `r icd_row("ICD10CM")$n_condition_records_in_data` condition
records with an ICD-10-CM source code.

The ICD-10-CM mapping below comes from the vocabulary alone, not from the data.
`r length(unique(icd10cm_map$icd10cm_code[icd10cm_map$in_breast_cancer_set == 1]))` ICD-10-CM codes map into the breast
cancer set through "Maps to". `r length(unique(icd10cm_map$icd10cm_code[icd10cm_map$in_breast_cancer_set == 0]))` codes
in the C50 category map somewhere outside it. The full list is in
`codelists/breast_cancer_icd10cm_map.csv`.

## Cohort (M3)

```{r}
attrition_sql <- results("m3_attrition_sql.csv")
attrition_cc  <- results("m3_attrition_cohortconstructor.csv")
cohort_sum    <- results("m3_cohort_summary.csv")

summary_value <- function(variable, level = "") {
  cohort_sum$value[cohort_sum$variable == variable & cohort_sum$level == level]
}
```

The index date is the first breast cancer record inside an observation period.
People need at least 365 days of observation before it and must be 18 or older
on it. Sex is recorded and not filtered on. The cohort ends at the end of the
observation period.

The cohort is built twice, once with the SQL in `sql/cohort/` and once with
CohortConstructor in `R/30_cohort.R`. A test checks that both give the same
people with the same start and end dates.

### Attrition

```{r}
gt(attrition_sql) |>
  cols_label(step = "Step", description = "Step description",
             n_persons = "Persons", n_records = "Records") |>
  fmt_integer(columns = c(n_persons, n_records))
```

CohortConstructor records its own steps, with more detail.

```{r}
gt(attrition_cc[, c("reason", "number_subjects", "number_records")]) |>
  cols_label(reason = "Step", number_subjects = "Persons",
             number_records = "Records") |>
  fmt_integer(columns = c(number_subjects, number_records))
```

The prior-observation rule removes
`r num(summary_value("excluded_for_prior_observation", "persons"))` people.
`r num(summary_value("excluded_for_prior_observation", "with_0_prior_days"))` of
them have their breast cancer record on the first day of their observation
period, with no observation before it. The median prior observation among the
people removed is `r summary_value("excluded_for_prior_observation", "median_prior_days")` days.

### The cohort

The cohort holds `r num(summary_value("persons"))` people:
`r summary_value("sex", "FEMALE")` female and `r summary_value("sex", "MALE")` male.
Median age at index is `r summary_value("age_at_index", "median")` years
(range `r summary_value("age_at_index", "min")` to `r summary_value("age_at_index", "max")`).
Index dates fall between `r summary_value("index_year", "min")` and
`r summary_value("index_year", "max")`.
